hero.title: The Noble Eightfold Path (Ashtangika Marga)
hero.description: The fundamental core of Buddhist ethics and spiritual discipline prescribed by Gautama Buddha to achieve Nirvana.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Context

  • Part of the 4th Noble Truth
  • Sermon: Dhammacakkappavattana
  • Location: Deer Park, Sarnath

Pillars

  • Panna (Wisdom)
  • Sila (Conduct)
  • Samadhi (Concentration)

The Mindmap of the Eightfold Path

  • Group 1: Wisdom (Panna)
    • Right View (Samma Ditthi): Understanding the 4 Noble Truths.
    • Right Resolve (Samma Sankappa): Intention of renunciation, goodwill, and harmlessness.
  • Group 2: Ethical Conduct (Sila)
    • Right Speech (Samma Vaca): No lying, harsh speech, or gossip.
    • Right Action (Samma Kammanta): No killing, stealing, or sexual misconduct.
    • Right Livelihood (Samma Ajiva): Earning a living without harming others.
  • Group 3: Mental Discipline (Samadhi)
    • Right Effort (Samma Vayama): Developing wholesome states.
    • Right Mindfulness (Samma Sati): Awareness of body, feelings, and mind.
    • Right Concentration (Samma Samadhi): Achieving deep meditative states (Jhanas).

cards.details: Gautama Buddha delivers the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta at Sarnath, introducing the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.
Ashoka the Great popularizes these teachings through Edicts, formalizing the Dhamma as a state ethic.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing the Eightfold Path with the Four Noble Truths. The Path is the fourth Truth (Magga).
Assuming the Path is only for monks; historically, Buddha preached the 'middle path' for laypeople as well to achieve a better rebirth.
Equating 'Right Action' strictly with non-violence (Ahimsa), though non-violence is core, the path includes specific ethical conduct regarding theft and sexual behavior.
